issues: Broken Markdown/list structure: the translated text contains a duplicated block of headings and the 'Considering' section; the first occurrence also merges the end of item (a) with a new '# REGENT OF SOUTH BUTON' heading (missing line break/semicolon).
Meaning/structure drift: due to duplication and the missing terminator in the first 'Considering' item (a), the document boundaries and list item integrity are corrupted for downstream splitting.

Meaning drift: 'pemenuhan hak asasi manusia atas tindak kekerasan perempuan dan anak' was mistranslated as 'fulfill human rights against acts of violence...' (should be fulfillment of human rights in relation to/for victims of violence against women and children).
Meaning drift: 'Perlindungan Terhadap Saksi dan Saksi Korban' was mistranslated as 'Protection of Witnesses and Victim Witnesses' (should be 'Witnesses and Victims').

Scrambled/merged list markers in multiple articles: conjunctions and item letters are stuck together (e.g., "andf.", "and/org.", "andj.", "andb.") and some items run on in the same line as the preceding item (e.g., Article 3 and Article 5). This breaks list structure required for downstream splitting.
Meaning drift/clarity issue in Article 2 item f: Indonesian "pengayoman" is better rendered as "protection/shelter"; keep as "protection" but ensure it is a separate list item (structure fix).

Broken/scrambled list structure: several sub-items (a–g) are run together with preceding text (e.g., Article 8(1) 'meliputi:a.', Article 9(2) 'meliputi:a.', Article 10 'untuk:' followed by 'a.' on same line; multiple places where 'and/or d.' etc. are not on their own list line). This risks downstream boundary splitting.

Main required fix is structural formatting to match original list markers and separation.

Minor marker punctuation mismatch: Article 16(1) item e ends with ':' in translation ('registration: f.') whereas original uses ';' and separate 'f.' item; needs separation to preserve list markers cleanly. նույնպես affects automated parsing.

Broken Markdown structure: the original has the heading "## Bagian Kesatu" (level-2), but the translation renders it as "## Part One" instead of keeping the same heading text structure (should be "## Section One" to match the original's sectional heading convention).
Meaning drift: "Bagian Kesatu" is a formal subdivision label; translating it as "Part One" changes the legal-structural term used for the subdivision (Bagian = Section).

Scrambled/merged list structure: several lettered items are run together (Article 20 items c–e; Article 21(2) items a and g; Article 21(3) items a and d; Article 22 paragraphs (1) and (2) and items b–d; Article 23 paragraphs (1) and (2) and item f; Article 26 items a and e).

Scrambled/merged numbering in the original is not mirrored: in Article 22 paragraph (2) is merged into paragraph (1) line in the original; translation separates it onto its own line, altering boundary/marker structure.
